displayQuote: There are two educations. One should teach us how to make a living and the other how to live

meta.title: Who really said "There are two educations. One should teach us how to make a living and the other how to live"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Not John Adams. Historian James Truslow Adams wrote it in his essay "To 'Be' or to 'Do'" in The Forum, June 1929. Popular versions also drop the word "obviously."
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'There are two educations. One should teach us how to make a living and the other how to live'?
meta.ogDescription: Not President John Adams: historian James Truslow Adams wrote it in The Forum, June 1929. The original says "There are obviously two educations."

answer.label: Not John Adams — actually James Truslow Adams
answer.sourceLine: Written by the historian James Truslow Adams, not by President John Adams. It appears in his essay “To ‘Be’ or to ‘Do’: A Note on American Education” in The Forum, June 1929, which we checked in a scan of the issue. His original sentence begins “There are obviously two educations.”

source.heading: The documented source

docMeta.dd: To “Be” or to “Do”: A Note on American Education
Shortened: drops “obviously” and the comma after “living”

source.excerpt: There are obviously two educations. One should teach us how to make a living, and the other how to live. Surely these should never be confused in the mind of any man who has the slightest inkling of what culture is. For most of us it is essential that we should make a living.
trail: Wikiquote’s sourced quotes for James Truslow Adams give the full passage and cite “To ‘Be’ or to ‘Do’,” The Forum, vol. 81, no. 6 (June 1929), p. 325. Wikiquote: James Truslow Adams ↗

The scan of the June 1929 Forum opens with “To ‘Be’ or to ‘Do’: A Note on American Education, by James Truslow Adams,” and the essay contains the sentence word for word, with “obviously.” Internet Archive full text ↗
Wikiquote’s page for President John Adams lists the line under “Misattributed” and credits James Truslow Adams. It notes the line is “sometimes rendered” without “obviously.” Wikiquote: John Adams ↗
Wikipedia’s article on James Truslow Adams says the quote “is widely misattributed to John Adams” and comes from his June 1929 Forum essay. Wikipedia: James Truslow Adams ↗
source.excerptNote: Transcribed from the scan of the June 1929 Forum on the Internet Archive. The essay then argues that training for a trade or profession is “merely learning how to make a living,” while a liberal education should teach people “how to live and how to get the best out of living.”

author.name: James Truslow Adams
author.heading: About James Truslow Adams
author.bio: James Truslow Adams was an American writer and historian, born in Brooklyn. He worked in investment banking before he became a freelance author. He won a Pulitzer Prize for History for The Founding of New England, and he coined the phrase “American Dream” in The Epic of America (1931). Wikipedia traces his family line to a Maryland settler, Francis Adams, and gives no link to the family of President John Adams.

misattribution.heading: Why it gets pinned on John Adams
misattribution.intro: Two famous Americans named Adams, and a line about education that sounds like a Founding Father: the sentence has drifted from a 1920s historian to the second president. On the way it also lost a word.

items.why: Quote sites and the press credit the president. For example, CBS News ran the shortened line as its “Quote for the Day” on October 16, 2006, attributed to John Adams. CBS News, 2006 ↗ Wikiquote lists it under “Misattributed” on his page. Wikiquote ↗

Some quote pages give John Adams’s Discourses on Davila as the source. One such page notes that the source “has not yet been checked against the original.” Example ↗ We searched the full text of the 1805 edition of Discourses on Davila and found no use of the word “educations.” 1805 edition on the Internet Archive ↗

The popular wording drops “obviously” and the comma after “living.” The 1929 original reads “There are obviously two educations. One should teach us how to make a living, and the other how to live.” 1929 text ↗

misattribution.truthLine: The author is James Truslow Adams, in “To ‘Be’ or to ‘Do’: A Note on American Education,” The Forum, June 1929. Wikiquote ↗

context.heading: What he was arguing
lead: The line opens a key passage in a 1929 essay that, as Wikipedia puts it, is “very critical of American education, both in school and at the university level.” James Truslow Adams called himself an outsider who had never been a teacher. He argued that schools and colleges were confusing two different goals. Wikipedia ↗

In his view, training for a trade or profession is useful but is “merely learning how to make a living.” A liberal education should help people learn “how to live and how to get the best out of living,” and he called that a lifelong task. The Forum, June 1929 ↗
context.pull: It is merely learning how to make a living.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote's James Truslow Adams page gives the full passage beginning 'There are obviously two educations', cited to "To 'Be' or to 'Do'", The Forum, vol. 81, no. 6 (June 1929), p. 325
Wikiquote's John Adams page lists the line under 'Misattributed', credits James Truslow Adams, and notes it is 'sometimes rendered' as 'There are two educations...'
The Internet Archive item is the June 1929 issue of The Forum, Vol 81 Iss 6

The full text of the June 1929 Forum contains 'To "Be" or to "Do" / A Note on American Education / by JAMES TRUSLOW ADAMS' and the passage 'There are obviously two educations. One should teach us how to make a living, and the other how to live...', plus 'merely learning how to make a living' and 'how to live and how to get the best out of living'

Wikipedia says the quote is widely misattributed to John Adams, comes from the essay in the June 1929 Forum, and that the essay is very critical of American education; it also gives JTA's 1878–1949 dates, the Pulitzer for The Founding of New England, the coining of 'American Dream' in The Epic of America (1931), and his ancestry from Francis Adams
CBS News 'Quote for the Day', October 16, 2006, gave 'There are two educations. One should teach us how to make a living and the other how to live.' attributed to John Adams
A quote page attributes the line to John Adams with the source 'Discourses on Davila, 1790' and notes that the source has not been checked against the original

In the full text of the 1805 edition of Discourses on Davila (Internet Archive item discoursesondavi00adam), the word 'educations' does not appear, nor do 'make a living' or 'how to live' (grep of the item's djvu text)
